flashcards.q: Core formulas: LTV, lifetime, payback months.
flashcards.a: LTV = ARPU x GM% x lifetime; lifetime ~= 1/monthly-churn (cap at 3-5 years); payback months = CAC / (ARPU x GM%). Example: $29 ARPU x 68% GM x 25mo (4%/mo churn) ~= $493 LTV.

LTV:CAC >= 3x screens healthy subscription growth; CAC payback within 12-18 months for mid-market SaaS. Below 1 destroys value per acquisition; above ~5 usually means underinvestment in growth or inflated inputs - audit before celebrating.

flashcards.q: Typical gross margins: traditional SaaS vs naive AI features?
flashcards.a: Traditional SaaS 70-85% (near-zero marginal copy cost); AI features naively 25-50% because every request burns tokens - marginal cost per user action returned. Cost engineering (cascades, caching) is how you claw margin back.

flashcards.q: Token cost per request: 1,200 input + 600 output at $3/Mtok in, $15/Mtok out?
flashcards.a: 1200/1e6 x $3 = $0.0036; 600/1e6 x $15 = $0.009; total $0.0126/request. Output tokens dominate despite half the count because they price 3-6x input - which is why output-length control tops the optimization list.

flashcards.q: Rank the inference cost levers by typical leverage.
flashcards.a: (1) Output-length control; (2) model cascades - small model handles 70-90% of traffic, frontier escalates hard cases; (3) prompt/semantic caching (repeated context steeply discounted); (4) distillation (5-20x cheaper serving); (5) batch endpoints ~50% off latency-tolerant paths.

flashcards.q: What is the cost-of-GOOD-enough knee and where do you operate?
flashcards.a: Quality improvements get more expensive per point while perceived value S-curves (below threshold trust breaks, above saturation nobody notices). Operate just past the perception knee: typically mid-tier + retrieval + tight output specs within 2-4pts of frontier quality at 5-15x lower cost, escalating rare/uncertain cases to frontier.

flashcards.q: Why must usage skew be modeled in AI unit economics?
flashcards.a: Real usage is heavily skewed: ~10-20% of users drive 50%+ of requests; P95 power users can cost 5-10x median. Median-only estimates understate COGS ~2-3x; power users on flat pricing can be negative-margin and are subsidized by light users - hence usage tiers/caps at ~P80.

flashcards.q: What goes into fully-loaded CAC that's commonly forgotten?
flashcards.a: Sales salaries + commissions amortized per deal, marketing tools/agencies, promo discounts and free-trial service costs (halve effective first-year ARPU), new-account onboarding/support hours, rising MARGINAL CAC with channel saturation. Organic users aren't free - attribute a shadow content/engineering cost.

flashcards.q: When is negative gross margin acceptable?
flashcards.a: Deliberately, temporarily, labeled: land-and-expand buying logos, marketplace subsidy phases, learning loops where usage IS improvement. Requirements: dated plan to positivity, monthly per-unit trend visibility, leadership agreement in writing. Indefinite negatives = burn with branding.

flashcards.q: 'Just wait for model prices to fall' - why is this weak?
flashcards.a: Prices fall ~10x per 18-24 months BUT usage grows faster than deflation when products succeed (Jevons), supplier concentration means your COGS follows their roadmap, and competitors get the same deflation. Underwrite at today's prices; treat deflation as upside.

flashcards.q: How do newer cohorts retaining worse than blended averages show up later?
flashcards.a: Blended LTV mixed aging enthusiast cohorts with worse-fitting scaled-acquisition cohorts; aggregates look fine until early cohorts age out of the denominator. Fix: cohort-and-channel-level LTV, pause channels whose cohort-LTV < CAC, feed retention back into targeting.

flashcards.q: Where does unit-economics framing NOT apply?
flashcards.a: Platform/infra investments arguing speed or risk reduction; compliance spends in risk terms; R&D bets with learning outcomes; loss-leader ecosystem plays. Choose the financial lens per decision type and LABEL it - what's banned is switching lenses when one loses.
